LanguageData.VCO_RestartTag_Tip: This one changes how the game loads its data, so it only takes effect after you close and reopen RimWorld.
LanguageData.VCO_RestartNeeded: Restart RimWorld for this setting to take effect.
LanguageData.VCO_Parry_Tip: When someone swings at your pawn in melee, your pawn can turn the blow aside with the weapon they are holding and take no damage.\n\nThey must have a weapon in hand. Better melee fighters parry more often, and a strong attacker is harder to parry. Attacks from directly behind can never be parried.
LanguageData.VCO_ParryFrontFactor_Tip: How easy it is to parry someone attacking you face to face.\n\nHigher means more parries. Lower means fewer.
LanguageData.VCO_ParrySideFactor_Tip: How easy it is to parry someone attacking from your left or right.\n\nThe default is 1.25, lower than the frontal value of 1.5, so gaining a flank weakens parries without preventing them outright.
LanguageData.VCO_ParryBudget_Tip: The most attacks one pawn can parry in a single second, no matter how skilled they are.\n\nThis stops one great fighter from holding off a whole crowd forever. It only starts to matter at roughly five or more attackers at once.
LanguageData.VCO_Counter: A successful parry lets your pawn hit back
LanguageData.VCO_Counter_Tip: After a successful parry, your pawn immediately gets a free attack against whoever swung at them.\n\nThis makes good melee fighters noticeably stronger.
LanguageData.VCO_PointBlank_Tip:
A skilled shooter stuck in melee sometimes fires their gun instead of swinging it.

Only pawns with Shooting 10 or higher can do this. The chance is 5% at Shooting 10 and rises to 50% at Shooting 20. The shot fires instantly at the pawn they were fighting, and otherwise works like any other shot from that weapon. It applies to everyone, including enemies.

Social fights, duels, finishing blows on downed pawns, and melee attacks you order directly always stay melee.
LanguageData.VCO_AdvancedArmor_Tip:
Vanilla armor rarely says no. Even a suit that beats the gun's penetration usually turns the hit into a bruise instead of stopping it. You only always bounce a hit when leftover armor (armor minus penetration) reaches 200%.

With this on, leftover 100% actually stops the hit. Armor that only matches the gun still does nothing, so a charge rifle still dumps a flak vest. The half-damage bruise still happens when leftover is lower than the stop point.

The gun's shown armor penetration is raised to keep weapons that already beat a plate beating it.
LanguageData.VCO_ArmorThreshold: Hits always bounce when leftover armor is {0}%
LanguageData.VCO_ArmorThreshold_Tip: Leftover is your armor percent minus the gun's armor penetration percent.\n\nVanilla always stops a hit at 200% leftover. Default 100% matches Vanilla Combat Reloaded: if the plate wins by that much, the shot does not go through.
LanguageData.VCO_PenetrationScale_Tip: Because leftover now stops hits sooner, ordinary penetration would bounce off plates it used to threaten. This multiplier is applied to the armor penetration shown on weapons and used in the armor roll.\n\nDefault 2 matches Vanilla Combat Reloaded. Raise it if guns feel too weak; lower it if armor feels too weak.
LanguageData.VCO_DirectionalDamage: Where you get hit depends on the angle
LanguageData.VCO_DirectionalDamage_Tip:
Normally a shot picks a random body part. With this on, the side an attack comes from decides what it can hit.

Shoot someone from their left and you can hit their left arm, left eye or left lung, but not their right ones. The torso can be hit from any angle.

This applies to guns and bows. Turn on the option below to include melee too.
LanguageData.VCO_MeleeFlanking: Apply this to melee attacks too
LanguageData.VCO_MeleeFlanking_Tip: Melee attacks also hit the side they come from, not just guns and bows.
LanguageData.VCO_HeightTargeting: Skilled drafted pawns can aim high or low
LanguageData.VCO_HeightTargeting_Tip: Drafted colonists with Shooting 10 or higher get a gizmo to aim at the head, torso or legs. Greater skill raises the chance of actually landing there; a miss still hits that side of the body, just not the band you asked for.\n\nEnemies with Shooting 10 or higher pick a random height when they spawn. Explosives ignore this.
LanguageData.VCO_CommandSetHeight_Tip: Weight incoming hits toward this height band. Requires Shooting 10 or higher. None is vanilla, any height.
LanguageData.VCO_ProjectileWounds_Tip: Bullets fragment, pass through or mushroom according to their stopping power. Arrows can stab inward or slice across adjacent outer parts.
LanguageData.VCO_BulletWorker: Bullets fragment, pass through or mushroom
LanguageData.VCO_BulletWorker_Tip:
Stopping power shapes the wound instead of only staggering small pawns.

Below 1 (pistols): the round fragments across nearby parts.
1 to 1.5 (rifles): it passes through from the organ to the outer part covering it.
Above 1.5: it mushrooms, dumping extra damage into one part.

A vest that already reduced the hit cancels all of this, so armor that catches the round also stops the extra trick.
LanguageData.VCO_BulletStoppingPowerCap_Tip: Mushrooming multiplies damage by stopping power. This is the ceiling, so an outlier stat cannot one-shot everything. Default 10 matches Vanilla Combat Reloaded.
LanguageData.VCO_ArrowWorker: Arrows stab through or slice across
LanguageData.VCO_ArrowWorker_Tip: Arrows get a stab's chance to force an internal hit. If they stay external they split most of the damage across two adjacent outer parts, so a graze is a slice rather than a single puncture.
LanguageData.VCO_AdvancedAccuracy: Skilled shooters overcome bad weapons and weather
LanguageData.VCO_AdvancedAccuracy_Tip: A good shooter partially overcomes penalties from a poor weapon at range and from bad weather.\n\nCover, smoke and target size are not affected — only equipment and weather factors.
LanguageData.VCO_AccuracyScale_Tip: How strongly shooting skill mitigates weapon and weather penalties.\n\nLower values make each point of skill matter more. Default 5 matches Vanilla Combat Reloaded.
LanguageData.VCO_Evasion: Moving pawns are harder to shoot
LanguageData.VCO_Evasion_Tip: A pawn who is running is harder to hit than one standing still.\n\nStanding still gives no benefit, so this is a trade: move and be safer, or stand and shoot back.
LanguageData.VCO_EvasionFactor_Tip: Each step of movement speed above the minimum multiplies hit chance by this value.\n\nLower means running pawns are harder to hit. Default 0.8 matches Vanilla Combat Reloaded.
LanguageData.VCO_EvasionMinSpeed_Tip: Movement speed below this gives no evasion benefit. Default 2.5.
LanguageData.VCO_EvasionSkillContest_Tip: When advanced accuracy is on, a skilled shooter's evasion mitigation also applies against moving targets.\n\nRequires skilled shooters overcome bad weapons and weather to be enabled.
LanguageData.VCO_FiringArc: Missed shots spread out with distance
LanguageData.VCO_FiringArc_Tip: Normally a missed shot lands somewhere near the target no matter how far away the shooter is. With this on, misses spread out in a cone, so shots from far away go much wider.\n\nThis makes long range shooting less reliable and closing the distance more worthwhile.
LanguageData.VCO_FiringArcDegrees_Tip: How wide the cone of missed shots is. Bigger numbers mean misses land further from the target.
LanguageData.VCO_FiringArcType_Tip:
How the cone is applied. Type 0 (default) widens freely with distance, matching Vanilla Combat Reloaded's stock setting.

1: same, but the miss radius never exceeds 10.
2: stops growing once the cone is as wide as a vanilla miss.
3–5: various caps on the near and far radius. Leave this at 0 unless you know you want a tighter long-range miss.
LanguageData.VCO_VisibleTracers_Tip:
Vanilla bullets are a one-pixel speck. This draws a short glowing streak behind each projectile so you can see the shot.

Colour follows the damage: bullets yellow, arrows orange, fire red, stun cyan. Shells and grenades are left alone.

Combat Extended's Vibrant Tracers does the same job by swapping ammo textures. This is that idea for vanilla, without needing CE calibres.
LanguageData.VCO_TracerScale_Tip: How big the streak is, as a multiple of the default. Length and thickness scale together.\n\nLeave this at 1 unless the streaks read too heavy or too faint at the zoom you play at.
LanguageData.VCO_Suppression_Tip:
Bullets and explosions landing near an enemy of the shooter build suppression. Suppressed pawns aim worse and take longer to aim. Pinned pawns are hit harder by both.

How much depends on the shot's damage, how close it lands, and the target's nerves and mood. Explosions and the Suppression fire mode suppress more. Active shield belts, mechanoids and animals are unaffected.

Suppression fades a second after the shooting stops.
LanguageData.VCO_SuppressionPinning_Tip: When an enemy or ally is pinned, it stops what it is doing and moves to nearby cover for a few seconds before carrying on.\n\nYour own colonists are never taken out of your control: they only aim worse.
LanguageData.VCO_SuppressionStrength_Tip: Multiplies how much suppression each shot causes. Higher pins pawns sooner.
LanguageData.VCO_FireModes: Drafted pawns can choose a fire mode
LanguageData.VCO_FireModes_Tip:
Drafted colonists with a gun get a fire mode button.

Precision: better aim, slower to aim, smaller bursts.
Short Burst: a few extra rounds, slightly worse aim, quicker to fire.
Suppression: many more rounds, much worse aim, fast to aim but slow to recover.
Auto: picks one of those by distance to the target.

The mode only applies while drafted, so hunting and undrafted self-defence fire normally. Explosives, one-use launchers and abilities are never affected, and single-shot and beam weapons only offer Default and Precision.
LanguageData.VCO_FireModesNpc: Other factions use fire modes too
LanguageData.VCO_FireModesNpc_Tip: Raiders, visitors and allies pick a fire mode by distance, the same way a colonist on Auto does.
LanguageData.VCO_FireModeShortBurstRange: Auto uses Short Burst from {0} cells
LanguageData.VCO_FireModeShortBurstRange_Tip: Targets closer than this get Suppression. Default 12.
LanguageData.VCO_FireModePrecisionRange_Tip: Targets at least this far away get Precision. It can never be closer than the Short Burst distance. Default 25.
LanguageData.VCO_FireModeAccuracy_Tip: Changes the shooter part of the hit chance as if the target were this many times closer. Above 1 aims better and below 1 aims worse.\n\nIt never raises a shot above certain, and it matters most at long range.
LanguageData.VCO_FireModeAimTime_Tip: Multiplies how long the pawn aims before the first shot.
LanguageData.VCO_FireModeCooldown_Tip: Multiplies the pause after a burst before the pawn can aim again.
LanguageData.VCO_FireModeBurst_Tip: Multiplies the number of rounds in a burst, rounded to the nearest whole round. Single-shot and beam weapons are unaffected.
LanguageData.VCO_FireModeBurstLimit_Tip: Caps the change to a burst, so a weapon that already fires long bursts is not doubled.
LanguageData.VCO_CommandSetFireMode_Tip:
Choose how this pawn fires while drafted.

Precision: better aim, slower to aim, smaller bursts.
Short Burst: a few extra rounds, slightly worse aim.
Suppression: many more rounds, much worse aim.
Auto: Suppression up close, Short Burst at medium range, Precision at long range.
LanguageData.VCO_ApparelCoverage_Tip: Applies the complete coverage pack: sensible protection for hands, feet and faces; corrected acid and thump armour types; and improved layering for glasses, masks, helmets and headsets.
LanguageData.VCO_Apparel_Intro: These are Vanilla Combat Reloaded's coverage and layering patches. They change how vanilla and DLC apparel sits on the body. Each one needs a restart except improved headgear layering.
LanguageData.VCO_HandFeetPatch: Armour on arms or legs also covers hands or feet
LanguageData.VCO_HandFeetPatch_Tip: Arm and leg armour also covers hands and feet. Gloves and boots that only cover those parts move to a layer that can be worn with the armour. Needs a restart.
LanguageData.VCO_AcidHeatPatch_Tip: Biotech acid damage is resisted by heat armour instead of sharp. Needs a restart.
LanguageData.VCO_ThumpBluntPatch_Tip: Vanilla thump damage is resisted by blunt armour instead of sharp. Needs a restart.
LanguageData.VCO_GlassesHelmetPatch_Tip: Glasses can be worn with helmets that only cover the upper head. Needs a restart.
LanguageData.VCO_NoseMouthPatch_Tip: The nose is protected by anything that covers the mouth. Needs a restart.
LanguageData.VCO_MaskPatch: Masks cover what they look like they cover
LanguageData.VCO_MaskPatch_Tip: Gas masks, visage masks, war masks and similar pick up the face coverage their graphics imply. Needs a restart.
LanguageData.VCO_HeadsetPatch_Tip: Gunlink, airwire and integrator headsets can be worn with a helmet. Needs a restart.
LanguageData.VCO_ArrayHeadsetPatch_Tip: The array headset sits on the eyes, and the mech commander helmet is treated as upper head, so they can be worn together. Needs a restart.
LanguageData.VCO_ApparelTweaks_Tip: Treats eye and mouth apparel as headgear for pawn generation, so pawns can spawn wearing glasses or masks with a helmet. Does not need a restart.
LanguageData.VCO_AutoEquip_Intro: Each colonist follows a loadout, chosen in the Loadout column of the Assign tab. A loadout sets which weapons the colonist may use, whether it carries a backup melee weapon, and which items it keeps in its inventory.
LanguageData.VCO_AutoEquip_Tip:
Colonists equip and upgrade their primary weapon, carry a melee sidearm and stock items as their loadout says. Selection considers damage, accuracy, armour penetration, condition, and the colonist's shooting or melee skill. Drafted colonists are never sent to fetch gear.

Manually equipping a weapon locks that choice until you use the colonist's Allow weapon upgrades command.

Turn this off to use another mod's loadout or sidearm system. The Assign tab column needs a restart to appear or disappear.
LanguageData.VCO_AutoEquipUpgradeMargin_Tip: How much better a replacement must score before a pawn changes an already-allowed weapon. A margin prevents repeated swaps between nearly identical weapons. Disallowed weapons can always be replaced.
LanguageData.VCO_AutoEquip_Unlock_Tip: This weapon was equipped manually. Remove that lock and allow automatic upgrades again.
LanguageData.VCO_Loadout_TitleTip: Loadouts set which weapons colonists use and what they carry. Assign them in the Assign tab.
LanguageData.VCO_Loadout_AutoPrimary_Tip: Colonists equip the best allowed weapon they can reach, and swap to a clearly better one when it turns up. Off: they keep whatever weapon you give them.
LanguageData.VCO_Loadout_CarrySidearm_Tip: Colonists with a ranged weapon carry the best allowed melee weapon in their inventory. When an enemy reaches them in a fight they switch to it, and switch back once the enemy is gone.\n\nDrafted colonists also get a button to switch by hand.
LanguageData.VCO_Loadout_SidearmOff: Colonists with this loadout do not carry a backup weapon.
LanguageData.VCO_Loadout_ItemsIntro: Colonists keep these items in their inventory, fetching more when they run low. They stop picking up items that would leave them over-encumbered.
LanguageData.VCO_Loadout_Disabled_Tip: Loadouts are turned off in the Vanilla Combat Overhaul settings. Restart to remove this column.
LanguageData.VCO_Loadout_Switch_Tip: Swap between the primary weapon and the backup weapon carried in the inventory.
